entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bretislaus II, who reigned as Duke of Bohemia from September 14, 1092, until his death on December 22, 1100, was a pivotal figure in the consolidation of Přemyslid ducal authority and the final suppression of paganism within his realm. The eldest son of King Vratislaus II and Adelaide of Hungary, Bretislaus's eight-year rule was marked by determined efforts to reform the Bohemian succession law and to eradicate lingering pre-Christian practices, firmly aligning Bohemia with Latin Christendom. His reign represents a critical juncture where the nascent Bohemian state solidified its internal structure and religious identity, impacting its trajectory within Central Europe.

During his ducal tenure, Bretislaus II confronted both external rivals and internal dynastic challenges. He actively pursued a policy against paganism, ordering the destruction of ancient sacred groves and the persecution of individuals adhering to old Slavic rites. A notable act was the expulsion of Slavonic monks from Sázava Monastery in 1097, replaced by Latin-rite Benedictines, symbolizing his commitment to Roman Catholic orthodoxy over the Slavonic liturgy. Crucially, Bretislaus attempted to replace the traditional senioratus (succession by the eldest male member of the dynasty) with primogeniture, aiming to secure the ducal throne for his younger brother Bořivoj II and prevent the fragmentation of power among numerous Přemyslid princes.
